tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...', 'Activate on requests like...'), focuses on user intent (reviewing/auditing sustainability posture, carbon footprint, etc.) rather than internal mechanics, explicitly enumerates many trigger phrases and contexts (including indirect ones like attaching a CSV export or asking about Graviton/AI workloads), and while lengthy, remains a single cohesive paragraph appropriate for the scope of a complex 29-practice review skill.
tests.evidence: "Use this skill when a user asks to review or audit a workload's sustainability posture, carbon footprint, emissions, water usage, environmental impact, or resource efficiency. Activate on requests like \"sustainability review\"..."

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense and domain-specific throughout — it does not explain general concepts (e.g., what CO2e or an API is) but jumps straight into project-specific conventions (e.g., reporting thresholds, attribution order, allocation rules) that the agent would not otherwise know.
tests.evidence: 'Absent or zero emissions are below the reporting threshold (0.5 g CO2e, 0.5 mL water), not zero impact. Carbon for month M publishes by the 21st of M+1...'

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The body references detailed data (metric names, API calls, thresholds) but keeps the actual detailed tables/lookups (KPI formulas, checklist of 29 practices, error tables) in references/ files, linking to them conditionally rather than inlining them.
tests.evidence: 'Load references/proxy-metrics.md. Over 30 days at Period: 3600, derive provisioned and utilized vCPU-hours...' — detail is summarized, full tables live in references/.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file in references/ is linked via markdown syntax in the body (workload-model.md, proxy-metrics.md, framing-and-attribution.md, emissions-collection.md, emissions-api-reference.md, csv-emissions-input.md, sus-best-practices-checklist.md, ai-ml-workloads.md, graviton-migration.md).
tests.evidence: 'Load [references/workload-model.md](references/workload-model.md)' and similar links for all nine reference files.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is tied to a specific step or condition that tells the agent when to load it (e.g., conditional on workload shape, before first API call, when CSV attached).
tests.evidence: 'ML / accelerated shape, or Invocations in the AWS/Bedrock namespace → load references/ai-ml-workloads.md.' and 'read references/emissions-api-reference.md before the first call.'

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference file links use relative paths rooted at references/ with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (API call sequencing, attribution order, emissions interpretation) are given exact prescriptive instructions, while flexible areas (scope selection, business metric fallback) explain reasoning and give fallback options rather than rigid steps.
tests.evidence: 'work through the ordered causes in framing-and-attribution.md before naming an architecture cause: comparison validity, methodology version, grid intensity...' vs. 'Ask for the scope ... default: all configured Regions'.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Where fallback options are given, a clear priority/default order is specified (e.g., business output metric fallback order 1-4, CSV override API only when attached).
tests.evidence: 'If there is none, use the first available fallback and state its caveat: 1. Request count ... 2. Invocation count ... 3. Data processed ... 4. None'

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable, repeatable review procedure (topology mapping, KPI derivation, practice grading) applicable to any workload, not a one-off declarative task tied to a specific resource.
tests.evidence: 'Walk the Agent Space topology from the entry point, classify every resource into a layer, and record each resource's Region.'

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The 'Critical — read first' section functions as a gotchas section, listing many concrete, non-obvious pitfalls specific to this domain (attribution mistakes, reporting lag, severity misinterpretation, etc.).
tests.evidence: 'Compare months per day. A 28-day month carries about 10% less than a 31-day one at the same usage; a delta smaller than the day-count difference is not a finding.'

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill produces a structured report and explicitly provides a template asset for this purpose.
tests.evidence: 'Load assets/report-template.md. Create one report artifact per workload...'

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large inline template exists in the body; the report template itself is stored in assets/ and only referenced, not embedded.
tests.evidence: 'Load [assets/report-template.md](assets/report-template.md).' — no inline template structure appears in the body.

tests.name: Asset files must be linked
tests.reasoning: The single asset file report-template.md is explicitly linked in the body multiple times.
tests.evidence: '[assets/report-template.md](assets/report-template.md)' appears in the Critical section and in Step 9.

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: The asset link specifies exactly when to load it — at Step 9, when creating the report artifact — satisfying the 'when to load' requirement.
tests.evidence: 'The report artifact is the deliverable. Create it with assets/report-template.md at Step 9 even when the user asks specific questions...'

tests.name: Asset path format
tests.reasoning: The asset reference uses a relative path from the skill root with no absolute path or traversal.

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: The workflow is presented as an ordered checkbox checklist with Step N labels, and detailed sections below reference the same step numbers (### Step 1 — Scope..., ### Step 2 — Topology, etc.), matching the required format.
tests.evidence: '- [ ] Step 1: Scope and business output metric' ... '### Step 1 — Scope and business output metric'

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The skill includes an explicit self-validation checklist before presenting the report, checking for completeness, consistency, and correctness of the output.
tests.evidence: 'Before presenting the report, check the draft and fix any failure: - [ ] All 29 practices have a status, and every MET cites evidence. ... - [ ] No recommendation states impact in MTCO2e...'
